$comment: sandbox-breach catalog. Two legs, used for the A/B susceptibility comparison the demo runs:
'local/*' (Dynamo-served Qwen, discovered at runtime via ROUNDHOUSE_LOCAL_* env vars -- not
listed here, same as openjev-demo's catalog; see that use case's README) and the frontier
entry below, azure/anthropic/claude-opus-5 via NVIDIA's inference-api gateway.
The user's own sample code called this model through the OpenAI Chat Completions dialect
(client.chat.completions.create(...)), but this roundhouse build's FrontierClients registry
(crates/roundhouse-server/src/main.rs, frontier_clients()) only has real dispatch clients for
openai_responses and anthropic_messages -- openai_chat_completions is a valid WireProtocol
variant (used for cross-dialect translation) but has no upstream client, and boot refuses
with 'this build has no client for that dialect' if a catalog entry names it. Verified
empirically (2026-09-29) that inference-api.nvidia.com/v1/messages accepts this exact model
string and answers with a real Anthropic-shaped message -- so this entry speaks
anthropic_messages instead, the same dialect cache-aware-routing's frontier entry uses at the
same base_url. Auth env is INFERENCE_API_KEY (not NVIDIA_API_KEY -- that name is already used
by breakout-lab's own memory-mcp server for its internal LangChain/ChatNVIDIA calls, which are
out of roundhouse's scope entirely).
PRICES BELOW ARE PLACEHOLDERS, not a quote -- this catalog exists to route two legs of an
exploit demo, not to make a savings claim. quality_prior 0.95 is a hand-written placeholder
(opus-tier), not sourced from a published index; replace before trusting it for anything else.
local_quality's 0.72 for Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct is the same placeholder cache-aware-routing
and openjev-demo use (Option B, cache-aware-routing/INTEGRATION.md Gap 4).
